stories.Headline: Energy Is the Battleground of the AI and Robot Era, Experts Say
stories.Summary:
Hyundai Motor Group plans to invest about 9 trillion won in Saemangeum to build a physical AI ecosystem, an executive director named Moon Sung-hyup told the FES 2026 International Forum. The forum was held on a Monday at Jeonbuk National University and was hosted by the Jeonbuk State government with several co-organizers. About 300 experts and officials from industry, academia, research institutes and government attended. In February, the group signed a memorandum of understanding with the Saemangeum Development and Investment Agency and announced an investment plan worth about 8.9 trillion won.

The project has five pillars, including solar power worth about 1.3 trillion won, hydrogen production worth about 1 trillion won and an AI data center worth about 5.8 trillion won. It also includes a robot plant worth 400 billion won and a hydrogen AI city worth 400 billion won. The data center would have a capacity of about 165 megawatts and house roughly 50,000 GPUs. The electrolysis facility, at about 200 megawatts, would produce roughly 30,000 tons of green hydrogen a year. Moon said groundbreaking on the data center starts in 2027, with main projects to be completed by the end of 2029.

Moon said Saemangeum offers a site of about 120 million pyeong, renewable energy potential, plans to expand port, airport and rail facilities and flexible land use conditions. He said the robot plant will make robots improved by trained data, and data from cities and industrial sites will feed back into AI training. A survey found about 700 of the group's roughly 5,000 suppliers were willing to shift into robot components. Hwang Chul-ju of Jusung Engineering said the energy market in 2030 could grow to more than four times the size of the semiconductor market.

Kim Joung-ho of KAIST said semiconductors and energy will decide AI competitiveness, and he named memory, power, capital and human absorptive capacity as key bottlenecks. He said power supply and cooling would be crucial to industry growth and called for subsidizing students' token costs. Yoon Jae-yong of Seoul National University said Saemangeum's competitiveness depends on its ability to execute, not on how much renewable energy it produces. Liang Min of Stanford said data center power swings strain grid stability and called for operators to bear the cost of new power infrastructure.

Articles.Title: Energy Is the Battleground of the AI and Robot Era, Experts Say - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Forus Health, Eyebetes Foundation work on AI-based diabetes screening
stories.Summary:
Eyebetes Foundation, working with Forus Health, ran a pilot retinal screening programme during Mumbai's Ganpati celebrations at Siddhivinayak Temple and GSB Ganpati Mandal. The article, published on 5 October 2026, says the initiative offered free screening to devotees and was designed to reach more than 15,000 people. It used Forus Health's FH-POISE AI solutions to analyse retinal images and explore links to diabetes risk and HbA1c levels. The aim was to raise health awareness and bring preliminary screening into a community setting.

The technology uses a retinal image to estimate HbA1c levels and flag diabetes risk without a blood draw or laboratory processing, according to the article. The article stresses that an AI-generated estimate or risk indicator cannot replace conventional diagnostic testing. People found to be potentially at risk should have conventional HbA1c testing and consult a qualified healthcare professional. The article also says building datasets that represent Indian populations could matter for evaluating and refining how well such technologies work in the country.

Srinivasan Venkatakrishnan, Chief Technology Officer and Head of Research and Development at Forus Health, said the company was exploring how a simple retinal image could give insights that traditionally required a blood test. He said the retina gave a non-invasive view of the body's microvascular health and that AI could help turn this into meaningful screening support. Dr. Nishant Kumar, a consultant ophthalmologist and retina surgeon who founded Eyebetes Foundation, said diabetes was no longer only a metabolic concern but a major public health challenge affecting the eyes, kidneys, heart and nerves. He said AI-powered retinal screening was promising because it could make risk assessment quicker, non-invasive and more accessible.

The article describes the pilot as a way to bring health awareness into an everyday community event rather than requiring a separate healthcare visit. It says such models could be relevant for community health camps, workplaces, primary healthcare settings and mobile screening programmes, especially where awareness or access to diagnostic facilities is limited. It adds that clinical validation, representative datasets, appropriate referral pathways and clear communication about the limitations of AI insights are critical so that technology complements rather than replaces established medical care. The article does not say what happens next beyond these points.

Articles.Title: Forus Health, Eyebetes Foundation work on AI-based diabetes screening - Mint

stories.Headline: Hyundai Launches Three Units for 9 Trillion Won Saemangeum AI Project
stories.Summary:
Hyundai Motor Group said on October 30 that five affiliates, Hyundai Motor, Kia, Hyundai Mobis, Hyundai Engineering & Construction and Hyundai AutoEver, have confirmed plans to invest in the construction and operation of the Saemangeum AI data center. The decision comes eight months after the group signed an investment agreement with the central government and Jeonbuk State in February. A dedicated entity for the data center, which will account for about two-thirds of the total investment, launches next month. The group also opened an office that will lead permitting and construction on the ground.

The new entities are divided by role. A data center special purpose company will handle construction of the hyperscale facility and its infrastructure, and a GPU service special purpose company will bring in high-performance graphics processing units and supply computing resources. A solar power special purpose company with 200 megawatts of capacity was established in September, and building review procedures for the data center have begun. The group plans to complete detailed design and major permits and to start construction in March 2027, with full service targeted for early 2030. The Saemangeum data center aims to have computing capacity equivalent to 50,000 GPUs, and the group decided in October last year to adopt 50,000 of Nvidia's latest Blackwell GPUs.

The Saemangeum AI Valley is a self-sustaining, circular industrial complex spanning 1.124 million square meters that brings together an AI data center, a robot manufacturing cluster, solar power generation, a water electrolysis plant producing clean hydrogen, and an AI hydrogen city. The total investment is about 9 trillion won, including 5.8 trillion won for the AI data center, 2.3 trillion won for the electrolysis plant and solar power generation, 400 billion won for the robot manufacturing plant, and 400 billion won for autonomous mobility and the AI hydrogen city. The group expects the investment to generate about 16 trillion won in economic ripple effects and 71,000 direct and indirect jobs. Financing details are being worked out based on a memorandum of understanding on financial support signed in April with the Korea Development Bank, the Export-Import Bank of Korea and others.

Shin Seung-kyu, executive vice president in charge of the RH PMO, said the group plans to break ground first on an AI data center in Saemangeum, where large-scale data accumulation and training are possible, to internalize autonomous driving and physical AI technology. He said the HMG Saemangeum Office is a symbol of the group's commitment to pursuing the project without wavering. Vice Chairman Jaehoon Chang said that if interest and support from the government and the National Assembly are in place, more corporate investment could flow into Saemangeum. He said the group has been carrying out its planned projects without disruption since announcing the investment, and that the most important part is speed. The data center is the brain of the group's physical AI strategy, and its first use will be in autonomous driving development.

Articles.Title: Hyundai Launches Three Units for 9 Trillion Won Saemangeum AI Project - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: UK Pharmacies Warn of AI-Faked Photos in Weight-Loss Drug Requests
stories.Summary:
British pharmacies have warned that patients are using AI-altered photos to obtain weight-loss drugs such as Mounjaro and Wegovy, according to the National Pharmacy Association and a Financial Times report on the 30th. Some patients have hidden weights in their pockets to appear heavier, and others have submitted digitally altered images that enlarge their stomachs. The NPA said these "fake obesity" cases are rising as demand for the drugs grows. Obtaining the medicines through deception can cause serious health problems, with particularly high risks for people with eating disorders.

Guidance introduced about two years ago requires pharmacies to verify the weight of patients seeking obesity treatments through video consultations or checks of medical records. In Britain, adults with a body mass index of 35 or higher and at least one weight-related condition can receive some treatment through the National Health Service. Private providers can prescribe the injections to patients with a BMI of 30 or higher, and the threshold falls to 27 for those with a weight-related condition. A recent University College London study estimated that 1.6 million British adults used GLP-1 drugs in the 12 months through early last year, with most buying them through online pharmacies charging about 300 pounds a month.

Asan Bhatti, owner of the online pharmacy QuickMeds, said close inspection of manipulated photos can reveal warped door frames or shadows and lighting that do not line up. He said verifying eligibility from photos alone is becoming harder as AI editing tools grow easier to use, and stressed that GLP-1 drugs are powerful prescription medicines with risks and side effects, not a quick cosmetic fix. Sehar Shahid, a director at the NPA, said patients who may not be clinically eligible are using AI-manipulated photos to obtain obesity treatments, and said regulation needs to keep pace with technology to protect patient safety. Kerry Fleming of the eating disorder charity Beat said she had heard accounts of people obtaining the drugs easily after faking photos with AI, and noted that measures such as requiring real-time photos exist but are not in place at all pharmacies.

Roz Gittins, chief pharmacy officer at the General Pharmaceutical Council, criticized pharmacies that check BMI by phone or rely on photos and pre-recorded video. She said information provided by the individual, including weight, height and BMI, should be verified by a healthcare provider other than the pharmacy. The council, which inspects hundreds of pharmacies each month, warned that pharmacists who fail to accurately verify patients will face sanctions. The Royal College of Psychiatrists has also raised concerns that patients under its care could misuse obesity treatments.

Articles.Title: UK Pharmacies Warn of AI-Faked Photos in Weight-Loss Drug Requests - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Figma Bets on Design-Specific AI Agent as Quality Lags Speed
stories.Summary:
Figma, a collaborative software company that provides tools for designing and building digital products, held an interview with the Seoul Economic Daily on the 30th at the Mondrian Seoul Itaewon in Yongsan, Seoul. Renee Loh, Figma's vice president of sales for Asia-Pacific, and Chase Wilson, the company's director of developer marketing, spoke at the interview. Loh said that artificial intelligence now lets teams put together a first draft of a product faster than before. She said the problem is quality, because designing something at a level you can actually ship now takes far more time and effort.

According to a Figma survey, 51% of South Korean developers used AI on every project over the past year, the highest rate in the Asia-Pacific region. Among respondents who said AI affected their productivity, 27% reported that their time to launch a product had actually grown longer. Some 47% of respondents said the AI tools they use lack design context, and 62% said they still need six to 10 rounds of revisions before AI output can be applied to a live service. Figma said 40% of KOSPI 200 companies were using its tools as of the second quarter of this year, and its customers include KakaoBank, Woowa Brothers and NAVER.

Figma's answer is Figma Agent, which lets users enter instructions for the AI inside a design file to create or revise screens, drawing on design information a team has accumulated. It selects the AI model and tools suited to each task, including AI models Figma has developed in-house. Wilson described AI as the best tailwind the company has ever had and said Figma Agent contains all of the design know-how the company has built up. Loh said products meant for release are held to a very high standard in terms of user experience, attention to detail and understanding of the user, and that when design context is not conveyed, much more rework is required.

Figma is also promoting what it calls a full-stack creative canvas strategy, based on the view that design is a team sport involving developers, product managers and marketers. Loh said the company wants an environment where people from any role gather in one space to make decisions together and build the product. Figma recently set up a dedicated Korean-language support team to reinforce its push into the South Korean market. Loh said Korea is one of the fastest-growing markets in Asia-Pacific and builds ambitious products, and that Figma will reflect the needs of Korean customers in its products and expand its support.

Articles.Title: Figma Bets on Design-Specific AI Agent as Quality Lags Speed - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Chinese Spy Targeted Nvidia's Jensen Huang, U.S. Officials Say
stories.Summary:
U.S. intelligence agencies believe a Chinese national known as Alice Huang, also called Huang Le, built a close relationship with Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang and passed information to China, The New York Times reported on the 19th, according to the Seoul Economic Daily. She was a former senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company that buys Nvidia chips and leases computing capacity to Chinese companies. U.S. authorities placed her under electronic surveillance and found she was in contact with a U.S. citizen, and a procedure to unmask the person revealed it was Jensen Huang. Photos posted online in June 2024 showed the two at a bar in Taipei, Taiwan, after a local tech show, and they were also seen together in May 2025 leaving a restaurant after a business dinner. President Donald Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about a year ago but took no action.

Megaspeed is listed by Nvidia as a cloud partner, and a Malaysian affiliate of the company bought at least $4.8 billion worth of AI equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February this year. U.S. authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 on suspicion it smuggled Nvidia chips barred from export to China, and a Commerce Department site inspection found some equipment still in its packaging rather than installed in data centers. Nvidia is the world's most valuable publicly traded company, with a market capitalization of roughly $5.2 trillion. The Times reported that Jensen Huang personally lobbied Trump in 2025 when the administration was considering a ban on AI chip sales to China, and that Nvidia donated at least $20 million to Trump's White House ballroom fund and pledged to invest $500 billion in U.S. manufacturing. The Times said it could not determine what information Alice Huang passed along, and that it remains unclear which agency monitored her.

Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo said meeting customers is part of a chief executive's job and that Jensen Huang speaks with thousands of customer executives every year, adding that he was confident the U.S. government would have told the company if it had determined a particular individual posed a threat to American industry. Nvidia said Jensen Huang and Alice Huang had a routine business relationship. Liu Chang, a spokesman for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, dismissed the reports as groundless slander and defamation. Megaspeed said it was taking the matter extremely seriously and doing its utmost to establish the relevant facts, and that it was cooperating actively with the U.S. government investigation.

U.S. officials concluded that Jensen Huang did not know Alice Huang was a Chinese government spy, but some senior figures in the Trump administration question whether he could have been unaware of it, the Times reported. Authorities did not give Jensen Huang a defensive briefing alerting him that he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence service, and intelligence agencies sometimes skip such briefings when doing so could expose their surveillance to the spy. The White House is on alert that Alice Huang may have learned not only about Nvidia's technology but also about Trump's views on U.S.-China relations through Jensen Huang, and the Times said the issue is likely to come up when Trump visits China next month. Current and former U.S. officials told the Times that the close relationship between Trump and Huang is obstructing enforcement against chip transfers abroad, and that sanctions proposals involving Nvidia and China have been halted within the Commerce Department.

Articles.Title: Chinese Spy Targeted Nvidia's Jensen Huang, U.S. Officials Say - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: NIK C2: The new AI-enabled command-and-control framework
stories.Summary:
Cisco Talos said on October 29, 2026 that it had observed a new AI-integrated command-and-control framework in the wild called NIK C2. Talos attributed the framework to an unnamed threat actor and said the actor had abused the OpenAI Chat Completions API. The framework includes a Go-based, 64-bit Windows implant that gives persistent control over compromised hosts. Talos said it saw the framework hosted on a server at IP address 87.120.196[.]120, which resolved the domain total-sitevv[.]lol, and that the server's certificate had the common name nik-panel, matching strings in the implant. Talos said it assessed with moderate confidence that NIK C2 is not merely a proof of concept but a fully functional framework.

The implant communicates over TLS-secured WebSockets on port 443 and an HTTP fallback polling loop every 250 milliseconds, with traffic protected by AES-256-GCM encryption derived from a hardcoded seed. It routes traffic across three prioritized C2 tiers and carries over 52 commands, including credential dumping, keystroke streaming, RDP session hijacking, process hollowing and a screen-lock ransomware module that demands payment in Bitcoin or USDT. Its ai_generate command sends prompts to the OpenAI Chat Completions endpoint, using an actor-supplied API key or, if none is given, the victim's OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable, and it defaults to the model gpt-4 when no model is named. Talos said all observed binaries were compiled with Go 1.23.4, released in December 2024, and that the development spans at least three versions. The implant copies itself to %appdata%/Roaming/Microsoft/Network, sets Windows autostart registry entries and masquerades as svchost.exe or simvol.exe.

Talos, whose researcher Chetan Raghuprasad wrote the report, said the pace of capability addition across the three versions indicates a technically proficient team with prior malware operations experience that is actively expanding NIK C2 toward a full-service adversarial framework. Talos said NIK C2 collapses collection and exploitation into a single continuous session, erasing the offline processing delays that historically gave defenders detection windows. It said such AI-enabled frameworks require defenders to move beyond traditional detection and embrace continuous behavioral vigilance as the new baseline. The articles do not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: NIK C2: The new AI-enabled command-and-control framework

stories.Headline: Midstream Health, whose AI tools help 250 hospitals recover revenue from rebates and vendor and payer underpayments, raised a $20M Series A led by Valtrius (Will Maddox/Axios)
stories.Summary:
Midstream Health, an AI financial system for hospitals, raised a $20 million Series A round, President and Co-founder Venkat Mocherla told Axios Pro exclusively. The round was led by Valtrius, according to the reporting. The company's tools help 250 hospitals recover revenue from rebates and from vendor and payer underpayments. The story was reported by Will Maddox of Axios and dated Oct 29, 2026.

The money is meant to expand the company's platform, the article says. Midstream aims to help hospitals recover revenue and improve margins as health-care costs continue to rise. The articles give no other terms of the deal, such as the company's valuation or how the funds will be divided. They also do not say when the round closed.

Mocherla is named as the person who confirmed the round to Axios Pro. The articles quote him only briefly and do not include further remarks from him or from Valtrius. No other executives, investors or hospital customers are named or quoted. The reporting does not say who else took part in the round beyond Valtrius leading it.

The context given is that health-care costs keep rising, which is why Midstream says it wants to help hospitals recover revenue and improve margins. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the plan to expand the platform. They give no timeline for that expansion and no details on hiring or new products. No further funding plans are mentioned.

Articles.Title: Midstream Health, whose AI tools help 250 hospitals recover revenue from rebates and vendor and payer underpayments, raised a $20M Series A led by Valtrius (Will Maddox/Axios)

stories.Headline: SpaceX Wins Target Lift On AI, Data Center Growth. But Is It A Buy?
stories.Summary:
SpaceX, the company owned by Elon Musk, is reportedly buying 418 homes in the Colonial Hills neighborhood of Southaven, according to a Guardian report published on October 29, 2026. Real estate agents have gone door to door offering owners deals on behalf of the company, and 18 homeowners have reportedly agreed already. The homes sit about half a mile from the power plant SpaceX uses for its data centers in the area. The catch is that sellers must sign an agreement not to join a class-action lawsuit over noise from the gas turbines.

The buyout covers an entire neighborhood, and the company says it needs the property for business purposes. Southaven mayor Darren Musselwhite said the homes will house SpaceX staff as the company expands, and he said the buyout is not meant to turn Colonial Hills into a company town. He described it as a goodwill gesture from a good corporate citizen for residents who see the nearby industrial development as negative. MZX, the SpaceX subsidiary that runs the Colossus II site, sent nearby residents an open letter saying it requires property for its business purposes.

The company has denied the allegations against it, saying it has adjusted power output and installed sound-dampening walls. Musselwhite said city monitors have not found the site breaching the local limit of 70 decibels, though some experts say persistent noise as low as 50 decibels could harm health. Residents described continuous noise like an airplane engine, with one piano teacher saying she has been woken at 2am and 3am. A plaintiff named Jason Haley said the sound has been so torturous he cannot sleep.

SpaceX has promised to remove all its unpermitted turbines within a year, especially as its 1.2-gigawatt power plant comes online, but the articles say this has not resolved the noise complaints. Separately, SpaceX and Tesla formed independent committees to study a possible merger, with SpaceX valued at $2.1 trillion and Tesla at $1.5 trillion. The two firms are co-building a chip plant called Terafab that could cost $119 billion. The articles say a merger could face political scrutiny from Beijing and Washington over data privacy issues.

Articles.Title: Stroll around the neighborhood: Opinions on AI and Data Centers

stories.Headline: AI in HR: The Future of Work Starts Now Professionals In Human Resources Association
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence is already in the workplace rather than something arriving someday, according to the article. Across organizations of every size, it is changing how teams communicate, recruit talent, analyze information, create content, and complete everyday tasks. Work that once took hours can now be done in minutes, freeing people to spend more time on strategy, relationships, and decisions that need a human touch. The article was published by Santa Clarita Magazine on October 31, 2026.

Adopting AI is not simply about finding the newest tool, the article says. As employees increasingly turn to AI platforms during the workday, organizations face questions about what information is safe to share and how to protect confidential employee and company data. They also face questions about what happens when AI-generated information influences a workplace decision, and whether they have a policy on how employees should and should not use these tools. The article says the organizations that benefit most will not necessarily be those that adopt AI fastest, but those that learn to use it productively, thoughtfully, and responsibly.

PIHRA Santa Clarita, a local chapter of the Professionals In Human Resources Association, is bringing local professionals together to explore what is changing, practical AI tools that can save time, ways to protect sensitive information, and considerations for responsible workplace AI guidelines. The chapter was established in 1992 by local HR professionals and has spent more than three decades providing professional development, education, and networking for HR professionals throughout the Santa Clarita Valley and surrounding communities. The article says navigating the future of work should not happen alone, and that HR professionals, business owners, executives, and people managers can all benefit from learning alongside others facing the same challenges. It invites readers to join the conversation and help shape what comes next.

Articles.Title: AI in HR: The Future of Work Starts Now Professionals In Human Resources Association

stories.Headline: The End Of The Human Internet? How AI Agents Are Rebuilding The Web Around Machines - OpEd
stories.Summary:
AI agents that search, browse, fill forms and transact for users are challenging the idea that humans are the internet's main audience. Cloudflare reported a more than 1,700 percent increase in AI-agent requests over the past year. It also said more than half of traffic on its network is now non-human. In September, OpenAI introduced new autonomous agent capabilities designed to pursue goals across applications. Other companies are developing systems that can plan trips, shop for groceries and manage subscriptions.

The shift threatens publishers because users may get a synthesized answer without visiting the sites the information came from, costing page views and advertising or subscription revenue. Chartbeat data reported by Axios showed significant declines in referral traffic from traditional search engines, particularly for smaller publishers. Axios later reported that traffic to news sites is falling as users move toward AI interfaces. Cloudflare has given website owners separate controls for search, AI training and AI-agent traffic. It has also introduced a system that can let publishers receive payment when AI systems use their content.

Cloudflare describes AI systems as a second audience for the internet and says the emerging agentic internet must be readable, discoverable, callable and payable. Visa has said transactions initiated by AI agents could become a major financial category, and retailers are experimenting with ways to allow or restrict autonomous purchasing. The article says the deeper issue is who controls the relationship between humans and information, since agents may increasingly decide which pages to read and which products to compare. It warns that AI-generated content is becoming abundant while agents consume material produced by other AI systems, so provenance may become as important as content itself. The article concludes that the human internet is not disappearing, but its architecture is changing rapidly.

Articles.Title: The End Of The Human Internet? How AI Agents Are Rebuilding The Web Around Machines - OpEd

stories.Headline: Neuron-Derived AI Video Model: 5x Faster Claim [2026]
stories.Summary:
The Biological Computing Co., a San Francisco startup known as TBC, released an image-to-video model called TBC mischief 1 on October 30, 2026. The company said in a PR Newswire announcement that it is the world's first publicly available neuron-derived AI video model. The model is built on Wan 2.2, an open-weight video model that TNW describes as Alibaba's, and TBC says it added an optimization layer that makes the existing model faster and cheaper to run. The model went live on two AI marketplaces, fal and OpenRouter, and an AWS Marketplace listing is marked as coming soon. Alex Ksendzovsky is co-founder and CEO, and Jon Pomeraniec is co-founder and COO.

TBC says the model generates video about five times faster than Wan 2.2 at comparable quality, with inference costs 80% lower. Pricing starts at half a cent per second of output at 480p and one cent per second at 720p, so a five-second clip costs 2.5 cents at 480p and 100 such clips cost $2.50. Clips run 3 or 5 seconds, at 480p or 720p in landscape, at 16 frames per second, delivered as MP4. TBC says the software layer adds less than 0.1% to the base model's parameter count. Tao Media cites a GPU benchmark of 142 seconds for Wan 2.2 versus 12 seconds for mischief 1, a ratio of roughly 12x, but the article uses the more conservative 5x figure because the public record does not explain the gap.

TBC says the biological neurons are not part of the shipped model and stay in its laboratory, with the findings converted into software add-ons for standard AI chips. Justin Hackney, co-founder of Wonder Studios, said the model's speed and low cost let his team push their work much further within the same time. TNW pointed out that the company has not published independent tests backing the speed claim, and the article says everything performance-related traces back to TBC. The one claim corroborated across independent outlets is structural: the product is software, and the neurons stay in the lab.

The article says building on Wan 2.2 lets TBC skip the cost of pretraining a video foundation model and compete on price rather than raw capability, but it also ties TBC's fortunes to someone else's release cycle. If the open-weight base improves, TBC must re-apply its layer to stay current, and if a new open model arrives with built-in speed gains, the pitch narrows. The article says buyers should check the Wan 2.2 license terms for themselves and should price the whole pipeline, including upscaling and human review time. It also says the 480p, 16 fps clips suit storyboards, previsualization, social loops and rapid concept testing, not a finished 4K commercial.

Articles.Title: Neuron-Derived AI Video Model: 5x Faster Claim [2026]

stories.Headline: Wisconsin AI Data Centers [2026]: $22B Spent, Only 1,500 Jobs
stories.Summary:
Microsoft finished the first phase of its Mount Pleasant campus in June 2026, and Vantage, Oracle and OpenAI started building in Port Washington, while Meta broke ground in Beaver Dam. The Lakeland Mirror had counted 44 AI data centers already operating in Wisconsin in December 2025 and reported seven cities had received proposals from unidentified companies for new campuses on farmland. Wisconsin Watch put Microsoft's Mount Pleasant complex at $20 billion and the Port Washington project at $15 billion, while Meta's Beaver Dam facility sits at $1 billion. The Milwaukee 7 regional economic development partnership, cited by Urban Milwaukee, estimated $22 billion of investment across the Mount Pleasant and Port Washington projects.

Milwaukee 7 projects more than 1,500 permanent jobs for Mount Pleasant and Port Washington combined once construction ends. Urban Milwaukee reports Wisconsin added 10,500 construction jobs between August 2025 and August 2026, with construction accounting for about half of the 19,400 total non-farm jobs added, and total construction employment reached 156,500 in August 2026. A draft Public Service Commission report, via Wisconsin Public Radio, projects electricity demand to rise 40 percent by 2032, with 72 percent of peak load growth tied to the three active data center developments. Wisconsin Watch reports at least 24 communities had data center moratoriums by July 2026, typically lasting one year, and an April 2026 referendum in Port Washington now requires voter approval for any future tax incremental financing district above $10 million.

Dale Kooyenga of the Metropolitan Milwaukee Association of Commerce said the state's economy would not be growing at the same rate without the two large projects. Scott Hodek of the Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development called the construction growth a generally good sign, and Brendan Conway of WEC Energy Group said the new power generation facilities his company is building are creating jobs too, with WEC reporting more than 3,000 workers employed in that construction. Amy Barrilleaux of Clean Wisconsin called the demand forecast shocking and said the state is in uncharted territory, while Conway pointed to more than $12.5 billion in solar, wind and battery storage investment planned by the utility. Tom Content of the Citizens Utility Board of Wisconsin argued that the state needs more oversight of the process.

The pattern in the reporting is that three hyperscale-style campuses are real and funded, while the long tail of proposals faces harder politics. Menomonie's pause and the Grant County debate show how fast a $1 billion-plus pitch can stall once residents learn the water and power terms, and the sources do not say what happens next for those proposals. The gap between the $22 billion figure and the roughly $35 billion implied by adding the two project figures probably reflects different scopes and phases, and readers should treat every dollar figure as a reported estimate, not an audited total. The sources also do not settle the gap between the $8 billion Lighthouse figure and the $15 billion project figure cited in 2026.

Articles.Title: Wisconsin AI Data Centers [2026]: $22B Spent, Only 1,500 Jobs

stories.Headline: Anthropic’s Claude slashes pharmaceutical document review times by 89%
stories.Summary:
Anthropic has expanded its use of the Claude AI model into pharmaceutical research, working with biotechnology companies on projects meant to speed up the creation of new medicines. The company described the work in a new blog post, saying it is looking at scientific and administrative obstacles in drug development, from molecular design to clinical trial preparation. The collaborations involve potential treatments for cancer, food allergies and rare muscular disorders, though most remain at experimental stages. At Generate Biomedicines, six scientists used Claude Code to modify a component of CAR T-cell therapy, which is traditionally used against blood cancers.

The redesigned component was about 70% shorter, which the company says creates more room for genetic instructions that could help the therapy address solid tumours. Laboratory experiments found that immune cells produced roughly ten times more cancer-detecting receptors. The modified cells also destroyed cancer cells more effectively and stayed active for longer periods, according to the reported findings. Generate Biomedicines reported a 70% reduction in the length of the CAR T-cell component.

Anthropic said the best way to identify and work through bottlenecks is to get deeply involved in real drug programs. The company has not said which of the treatments will move into further testing or when that might happen. The reported results come from laboratory experiments rather than human trials. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Anthropic’s Claude slashes pharmaceutical document review times by 89%

stories.Headline: BDC Q3 2026 deep dive: AI data centers and RUCKUS integration drive growth amid supply chain strain
stories.Summary:
Belden (NYSE:BDC) reported third quarter 2026 revenue of $966 million on October 31, 2026, up 38.3% from a year earlier and ahead of the $961.1 million analysts expected. Adjusted EBITDA was $171.1 million, a 17.7% margin and in line with estimates, and non-GAAP profit was $2.26 per share, matching consensus. The company guided fourth quarter revenue to $970 million at the midpoint, 0.6% above analyst estimates, and adjusted EPS to $2.28 at the midpoint. CEO Ashish Chand called it a record quarter, with bookings above $1 billion for the first time.

The quarter included the first contributions from the RUCKUS acquisition, and RUCKUS orders grew 10% year over year. Component shortages, especially for Wi-Fi 7 products in the RUCKUS segment, delayed some shipments and limited revenue. Belden signed a $100 million fiber solutions agreement for 2027, which it expects to lift its data center business by more than 50% to $275 million. Automation and smart buildings both posted double-digit organic growth, helped by large awards including high-speed rail and hospital projects.

Chand credited the company's network platform and growing customer base for the results, and management tied strong order momentum to AI data center offerings and large industrial and healthcare wins. CFO Jeremy Parks said component constraints may persist in the near term but that corrective actions are underway, and he described demand for Wi-Fi 7 and multi-gigabit switches as robust. Management called the RUCKUS shortages transitory, saying demand was under-forecast during the transition and that procurement fixes have begun. The company said RUCKUS integration is progressing, with joint commercial pilots and a push toward full-stack networking solutions.

Belden expects supply chain pressures to ease and data center revenue to rise significantly by 2027, targeting both core networking inside the data hall and broader campus infrastructure. It said it has secured supply contracts and internal capacity for that growth, and it expects RUCKUS shipments to improve in phases as procurement and combined supply chain management take effect. Management also pointed to a strong order funnel for large automation and smart building projects and to cross-selling between Belden and RUCKUS. The stock traded at $104.79, down from $106.66 just before earnings.

Articles.Title: BDC Q3 2026 deep dive: AI data centers and RUCKUS integration drive growth amid supply chain strain

stories.Headline: TWLO Q3 deep dive: messaging deceleration and AI adoption shape outlook
stories.Summary:
Twilio announced third quarter 2026 results on October 31, 2026, with revenue of $1.56 billion, up 19.9% year on year and above analysts' estimates of $1.51 billion. Adjusted operating income was $325.7 million, a 20.9% margin and a 12.3% beat. Non-GAAP profit was $1.65 per share, 12.4% above consensus. The company guided fourth quarter revenue to $1.6 billion at the midpoint, above estimates of $1.58 billion, and adjusted EPS to $1.51 at the midpoint, above estimates of $1.48.

Management pointed to broad-based product growth, with particular strength in voice and self-serve channels and continued expansion among independent software vendors. Messaging growth decelerated modestly from the first half of the year, which management attributed to tougher prior-year comparisons and some normalization after outsized gains. Voice delivered over 20% growth, helped by triple-digit growth in software add-ons like Branded Calling and Conversation Intelligence. Self-serve revenue growth exceeded 30%, and ISVs grew over 20%.

CEO Khozema Shipchandler said adoption of Conversations and Branded Calling lifted engagement but noted that AI-driven use cases in voice and consumer applications remain at an early stage. He said the technology adoption cycle will take time as consumers and businesses gain comfort. CFO Aidan Viggiano highlighted ongoing investment in higher-margin software add-ons and a focus on expanding gross profit through product mix improvement. Management cautioned that mainstream adoption among large regulated customers such as healthcare and finance will take time.

Management said voice AI and consumer agents remain at less than 1% penetration of total voice interactions. An identity validation offering is in private beta, with broader rollout planned for next year. The company expects higher-margin software products to become a more meaningful part of revenue, though seasonal factors and incremental carrier fees could pressure gross margins in the short term. Twilio trades at $199.81, down from $241.90 just before the earnings.

Articles.Title: TWLO Q3 deep dive: messaging deceleration and AI adoption shape outlook

stories.Headline: AI Is Changing What A Second Is Worth – OpEd
stories.Summary:
On October 30, the International Telecommunication Union issued its first major update to global precision-time guidance since 1997. Two weeks earlier, the body overseeing the world's measurement standards agreed to make Coordinated Universal Time continuous starting May 20, 2027, ending future leap-second insertions. These decisions change how the common reference clock is maintained, but they do not change the physical length of a second. The article says more accurate clocks improve measurement but cannot make a delayed observation current.

The piece says AI systems that act faster than evidence ages create a new risk, because synchronized clocks can still drive decisions on obsolete data, such as delayed sensor images or disrupted satellite-navigation timing. It gives the example of a robot in a container terminal acting on an old camera image after a worker enters a lane. It says the current second is defined by an exact frequency of 9,192,631,770 hertz tied to a transition in cesium-133, and that replacing that definition with an optical standard remains under development, with a possible decision in 2030. It notes that NIST's WWV shortwave station is extremely accurate at its transmitter, but reception for most U.S. users is generally accurate to within about 10 milliseconds. It also cites a 2024 Nature study in which machine learning helped lock lasers in three compact optical clocks that operated at sea for 20 days.

The author, Burak Oktenli, argues that critical-infrastructure procurement should require tested timing integrity, covering authoritative sources, maximum error, evidence age and safe behavior under failure. He says AI's authority to act should shrink when clocks or data are no longer reliable. He writes that systems need to know when the evidence behind a decision has become too old to trust, and that acceptable data age varies by setting, from hours for warehouse records to milliseconds for a moving machine near a person. He says some protective actions must execute immediately, so designs should define in advance which actions may proceed, which fall back to a narrower safe mode and which must wait for fresh data. He adds that human review needs a credible window to intervene before an action becomes irreversible.

The article cites the European Union Aviation Safety Agency's July update on satellite-navigation jamming and spoofing, and says EASA and EUROCONTROL are working on common procedures and training. It says NIST has mapped GPS timing use across telecommunications, electric power and financial services, and that the ITU's new handbook emphasizes terrestrial radio, satellite, optical-fiber and local time services. It recommends acceptance tests that introduce delayed messages, missing observations, inconsistent timestamps, interference and lost synchronization, plus audit trails recording capture time, source quality, processing delays and command time. It notes that NIST's positioning, navigation and timing risk guidance offers a foundation, though the proposed age limits are an engineering recommendation rather than an existing international mandate.

Articles.Title: AI Is Changing What A Second Is Worth – OpEd

stories.Headline: Sandisk (SNDK) Stock Sees Modest Fair Value Cut As Analysts Weigh AI Demand
stories.Summary:
Sandisk's modeled fair value was cut from US$2,173.00 to US$2,105.29 in an update published on October 31, 2026. The change came as analysts weighed enthusiasm about AI driven NAND demand against concerns about sector multiple compression. The article says the cut was modest and lines up with a mixed analyst backdrop. It also says the update reflects questions about how resilient today's conditions will be.

The update changed several assumptions behind the valuation. The revenue growth assumption moved from 40.74% to 27.18%, and the net profit margin assumption changed from 65.19% to 50.47%. The future P/E assumption adjusted from 11.02x to 12.21x, and the discount rate was updated from 8.53% to 8.48%. The article says the new figures point to a modestly lower price target.

Several firms, including Evercore ISI, Mizuho, Rosenblatt, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo, rate Sandisk as a key beneficiary of AI driven NAND demand, with Outperform or Buy ratings. Rosenblatt and Evercore point to the technology roadmap and the Kioxia partnership as support for competitive bit cost and performance. JPMorgan and Wells Fargo cite the new business model framework and non bit manufacturing economics as supportive of higher margins and reduced cyclicality. Morgan Stanley views the plan to return 100% of cash flow alongside moderate investment as a positive for capital allocation discipline.

On the other side, RBC Capital, Citi, Jefferies and Mizuho have trimmed Sandisk price targets over recent months. The article says they often point to sector multiple compression, more muted NAND pricing and questions about the durability of peak margin conditions. Jefferies flags investor focus on moderating pricing, lower gross margin guidance and possible near term headwinds from Edge inventory builds. Morgan Stanley is not fully convinced that industry improvements are more structural than cyclical.

Articles.Title: Sandisk (SNDK) Stock Sees Modest Fair Value Cut As Analysts Weigh AI Demand

stories.Headline: When AI Finds Bugs Faster Than The World Can Fix Them – Analysis
stories.Summary:
On 21 October 2026 European cybersecurity authorities issued a coordinated warning about two critical unauthenticated PHP vulnerabilities, software used in websites and business applications worldwide. Attackers could use the flaws to run code on affected servers without authentication. Security updates were available, but many organizations still had to work out which products contained the vulnerable component and whether a fix was compatible. The joint warning urged operators who could not update immediately to consider isolating exposed applications.

That same day OpenAI described a coordinated response involving AI-assisted researchers, independent security firms, PHP maintainers and infrastructure providers. OpenAI says one flaw was found with help from its model, while another research team independently found both, and the maintainers led the repair. The article says this showed defenders using AI to gain time but was not proof that every vulnerable server had been protected. It also cites Sam Altman at Stanford saying he no longer believed defenders could simply patch every bug. The EU Cyber Resilience Act has required manufacturers of covered digital products since 11 September to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents, with an early warning generally due within 24 hours and fuller notification within 72 hours, while broader product-security obligations take effect in December 2027.

The article argues that responsibility spans maintainers, distributors, suppliers, operators and governments, not just those who find flaws. It says critical-service contracts should specify who supplies fixes, for how long, how customers learn of affected dependencies, what temporary mitigation exists and how protection is proven. It calls for staged warnings through national incident-response teams, regional cybersecurity centers and large cloud providers, with disclosure timing judged on exploitation evidence, repair availability and the cost of delay. It also urges shared testing capacity for smaller operators and open-source maintainers, and says defensive AI should be a supervised aid rather than an unsupervised replacement for human-controlled deployment and rollback.

The article cites Britain's National Cyber Security Centre forecast through 2027 that AI would almost certainly make parts of cyber intrusion more effective and warned of a growing divide between systems keeping pace and those left more vulnerable. It points to the EU's 2026 threat landscape on geopolitical pressure, ransomware and interconnected dependencies, and to DARPA's 2025 AI Cyber Challenge finals, where automated competitors found 18 real vulnerabilities beyond those planted and supplied 11 patches for real flaws. It proposes measuring time to verified protection rather than time to a published advisory, including the residual exposed population and essential services that could not safely accept a fix. It describes OpenAI's Patch the Planet effort as an industry-led model open to independent scrutiny, and says a vulnerability is defeated only when dependent people and services can demonstrate they are protected.

Articles.Title: When AI Finds Bugs Faster Than The World Can Fix Them – Analysis

stories.Headline: 5 AI Side Hustles for 2027 That Are Worth Your Time
stories.Summary:
MoneyLion published an article on October 31, 2026, by Josephine Nesbit, edited by Ashleigh Ray, listing five AI side hustles for 2027. The article says most AI money pitches are noise or nonsense, and the real gigs solve a specific problem AI handles faster than a person alone. Each of the five uses AI for heavy lifting while a human supplies judgment, expertise or local know-how. Some are easy to start, while others reward years of hard-won expertise.

The first gig is AI automation, helping small businesses connect AI tools to email, bookings or customer records, and Deepanker Mahajan of SkillDrift said it needs only a laptop and paid plans for one or two tools. The second is AI training, where Ilia Lotov of Kaizen X Capital said professionals in finance, law, data science and sales can be paid to generate or assess content for models. The third is AI search optimization, and Matt Goren of RunOctopus said owners will pay someone to check and fix what AI tools say about their business. The fourth is AI-assisted content creation, and John Franco of GreenTek Roofing & Solar said he earned $46,000 over one year making faceless YouTube videos with AI tools. The fifth is building niche AI tools, and photographer Kristina Sherk used AI to create GenerAItion Headshots from her 20 years of experience.

Mahajan said connecting an AI assistant to a firm's systems still needs a person who understands how the business runs, and many small businesses have one repetitive task that takes hours every week. He said the real investment is your time, and you may have to do your first few jobs at a lower rate to have work to show prospects. Lotov said many AI companies pay substantial amounts for high-quality, human-generated data and hire experts to generate new content or assess AI content. Goren said more customers ask ChatGPT or Google's AI for the best plumber near them and go with the three or four names it gives, yet most owners have never checked what the AI says about them. Franco said the job is for everyone and needs only creativity, judgment and patience, but he stressed it is not easy money and human input matters.

The article's bottom line is that nobody needs a computer science degree, and what these gigs reward is knowing a specific problem well enough to fix it. It advises picking the gig that fits what you know, landing one or two clients and building from there. The article was provided by MoneyLion.com for informational purposes only and should not be construed as financial, legal or tax advice. The articles do not say what happens next beyond that.

Articles.Title: 5 AI Side Hustles for 2027 That Are Worth Your Time

stories.Headline: The Global AI Chip Race Needs Proof, Not Just Production – OpEd
stories.Summary:
On 23 October OpenAI reported that AI agents in separate virtual machines exchanged synthetic secrets through processor-cache timing without a network connection, according to an op-ed by Burak Oktenli. The experiment showed that software isolation does not fully prevent covert channels through shared hardware. Two days earlier, AI-assisted discovery of serious PHP software vulnerabilities set off an international patching scramble affecting government and other websites. Those were software flaws, not hardware attacks, the article says.

The article says procurement for critical systems should demand documented evidence of tested isolation claims, failure behavior and recovery paths. It cites research disclosed in 2025 and presented at IEEE Security and Privacy 2026, in which the Phoenix team at ETH Zurich found Rowhammer-induced bit flips in all 15 SK Hynix DDR5 modules in its test pool. Tripling memory refresh stopped the tested attack pattern at an 8.4 percent performance cost in the team's benchmark. The article also notes that the EU Cyber Resilience Act's reporting obligations have applied since September 11, with most broader requirements applying from December 2027.

Oktenli writes that suppliers should say which class of failure a security claim covers, under what assumptions and with what measured limits. He says buyers should ask which isolation claims were tested, how a platform behaves when memory integrity or firmware trust fails, and whether a system can recover without abandoning its mission. He argues that requirements should be risk-tiered, so a public website, a shared AI training cluster and an industrial controller are not forced into the same hardware design. He adds that independent laboratories can test defined claims without publishing sensitive exploit details.

The article points to DARPA's completed System Security Integration Through Hardware and Firmware program, Britain's CHERI research program and Arm's Morello development platform as serious work on stronger hardware. It says these are not universal cures and that claims should be matched to mechanisms. It also says Google DeepMind reports using AlphaChip to assist chip layout, though layout efficiency is not a demonstration of resistance to AI-assisted attacks. The article concludes that a chip's test record, not its country of origin, tells buyers what it can be trusted to protect.

Articles.Title: The Global AI Chip Race Needs Proof, Not Just Production – OpEd

stories.Headline: Trusted Human Context Emerges as a New Infrastructure Requirement for Enterprise AI
stories.Summary:
mEinstein, a company led by founder and CEO Prithwi Thakuria, issued a press release on October 31, 2026, from Boston, Massachusetts, saying that trusted access to human context is becoming a new infrastructure requirement for enterprise AI. The release says AI is moving from answering questions toward taking part in real-world workflows, and that the first phase of AI infrastructure focused on compute, models, cloud capacity and data. It says those layers remain essential, but capable AI systems still face a different constraint: understanding the relevant human context and knowing what the individual has authorized. The release was distributed through EIN Presswire.

The release says human context can include routine, mobility, health, financial patterns, household information, preferences, intent, readiness and prior actions. It says the emerging model, unlike traditional third-party behavioral data, emphasizes provenance, purpose, permission, revocation and user control. mEinstein calls this category Human Intelligence Infrastructure. The company says its architecture centers on a private, on-device Algorithmic Self-Portrait, an evolving representation of the user's real-world context, combined with a permission layer that governs what may be used externally, by whom, for what purpose and for how long. The company says it is also developing an enterprise architecture in which workflow requirements can be expressed as governed Human Context Contracts, with AI interpreting the request, deterministic policy governing execution, and approved context or action fulfilled at the user boundary.

Thakuria said AI can know almost everything about the world and still know surprisingly little about the human moment in front of it. He said context turns generic intelligence into relevant intelligence, and permission determines whether that intelligence can legitimately become action. He also said understanding a person is not the same as having permission to act for them, and that as AI becomes agentic, that distinction becomes infrastructure. The release says mEinstein's current enterprise work spans transportation, healthcare, clinical research and financial-services use cases, and that its live paid TxDOT/Jacobs Phase 1 is testing permissioned longitudinal mobility intelligence, while the same architecture is being explored through other regulated workflows.

The company says its architecture is still developing. The release says some core contract-to-device capabilities exist today, while agent-native intake, contract intelligence, workflow binding and automation remain areas of productization. It says the broader thesis extends beyond mEinstein, and that as model capabilities improve, AI systems may increasingly compete not only on intelligence but on their ability to access relevant human context under legitimate user control. Thakuria said the first AI infrastructure race was about creating machine intelligence at scale, and the next one may increasingly be about giving that intelligence trusted access to human context.

Articles.Title: Trusted Human Context Emerges as a New Infrastructure Requirement for Enterprise AI

stories.Headline: At Adipec, energy’s big chance to power the AI boom
stories.Summary:
Adipec, the annual energy gathering in Abu Dhabi, opened on Monday November 2, 2026, with artificial intelligence at the centre of its agenda. The four-day event has been held in the city every year since 1984. This year it brings together 2,260 exhibitors, 181,000 pre-registered visitors, 40 government ministers and 12,000 conference delegates. Organisers expect record numbers of delegates from Asian countries, whose demand for energy remains strong.

New research carried out jointly by Adnoc, XRG and Microsoft found that 62 per cent of surveyed energy leaders now rank AI among their two leading corporate priorities, up from 42 per cent last year. Almost nine in 10 of those leaders have increased spending on the technology, and 63 per cent expect returns on existing investments to cover or exceed their costs. Nearly three quarters of respondents expect AI to increase energy consumption by 2030, while only 52 per cent believe existing infrastructure can meet the extra demand. A separate Adipec survey found that 81 per cent of energy executives expect AI-related electricity requirements to exceed current forecasts.

The editorial says ramping up energy production can only partly meet this surging demand, and that investment is also needed to modernise grids, expand storage and accelerate cleaner generation. It points to Adnoc's work across the oil production ecosystem and to Masdar's ambitions in the US data-centre market as examples of how these developments are being taken into account. It adds that reliable supply will require a mix of technologies backed by infrastructure that can deliver electricity when and where it is needed. The piece describes AI as already improving maintenance, enhancing production, making hazardous inspections safer and helping balance complex electricity networks.

The gathering takes place amid uncertainty in global energy markets, which have been disrupted by geopolitical turmoil, including threats to shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz. The editorial notes that energy flows continue from the UAE and the wider region despite this. It says last year's theme was that power is now knowledge, meaning the electricity needed for AI processing, and that this equation is being tested by geopolitical strain and rising electricity demand. One of this year's themes, on performance under pressure in a new era, is described as highly relevant as the industry focuses on building resilience, and the editorial says it hopes the answers can be found at Adipec over the next four days.

Articles.Title: At Adipec, energy’s big chance to power the AI boom

stories.Headline: Website uses AI to help voters research candidates ahead of Election Day
stories.Summary:
A website called Elections Simplified is using artificial intelligence to help voters research candidates ahead of Election Day, CBS19 News reported on October 31, 2026. The site lets users search by address, city or ZIP code to find elections in their area, see who is running and review candidates' public records. It also provides campaign finance information and helps users understand how much their vote could influence different races. Shu Yang, a team member of Elections Simplified, said the idea came from his own frustration with trying to learn about candidates beyond campaign advertisements and political promises.

The site uses artificial intelligence to gather publicly available information in one place and summarize complex legal language, including ballot measures. Yang said the technology is meant to organize and explain existing information rather than generate new facts, and he stated that the AI does not generate or create anything. He added that the website's code is open source, allowing the public to review its algorithms and safeguards. Yang said local elections, including city council, school board and water district races, can be decided by relatively small numbers of voters, sometimes only a few hundred people.

Yang said he believes voters should focus on candidates' actions rather than their campaign messaging, and that the best way to know a person is by what they do, not what they say. He said the goal is to make researching candidates faster and more accessible, particularly for voters who may not have the time to search through extensive public records. He hopes the website will help people feel more informed about their choices and encourage them to participate in elections. Yang said he hopes to keep Elections Simplified running beyond the current election cycle, depending on available funding, and the website is available at www.ElectionsSimplified.com.

Articles.Title: Website uses AI to help voters research candidates ahead of Election Day

stories.Headline: Figma Opens Its Canvas to AI Coding Agents, Answering Canva's Pivot
stories.Summary:
Figma announced at its Config India event in Bengaluru on October 15, 2026 that it had added 20 new partners to its Model Context Protocol server. The partners include Amp, ClickUp, Dia, Junie by JetBrains, Linear, Meta Muse, Mistral, Notion, OpenCode and Sarvam Agents. The protocol lets outside AI agents read and write inside a Figma file, so tools like Claude Code and Cursor can query a file's layout, type styles, color tokens and component structure and then write changes back. Figma had already opened a narrower version of this in March with five partners focused on turning code into editable canvas objects.

Figma's help documentation lists Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code and Codex among the supported clients. Co-founder Dylan Field posted on X that MCP is not a perfect protocol, pointing out that Anthropic, which created the standard, does not expose artifacts and other cloud resources created through MCP calls. He said this leaves asymmetric context-sharing problems unaddressed. Figma reported Q1 revenue of $333.4 million, up 46% year over year, and raised its 2026 revenue outlook.

The timing follows Canva's move on April 16, 2026, when chief operating officer Cliff Obrecht told the Canva Create crowd in Los Angeles that Canva was shifting from a design platform with AI tools to an AI platform with design tools. Canva launched Canva AI 2.0 around its in-house Canva Design Model, which returns editable vectors from a plain-English prompt, and Obrecht called it the biggest product overhaul since Canva launched in 2013. Canva sits on roughly $4 billion in annual recurring revenue and a private valuation near $60 billion. Figma priced its July 2025 IPO at $33 a share and traded around $27 a share, with roughly $14 billion in market cap, by late August 2026.

Articles.Title: Figma Opens Its Canvas to AI Coding Agents, Answering Canva's Pivot

stories.Headline: Core Scientific (CORZ) vs. CIFR and WULF: Can Its Shift From Bitcoin Mining to AI Colocation Unlock Long-Term Value?
stories.Summary:
Core Scientific, known as CORZ, is moving from Bitcoin mining to renting data center space and power to AI companies. In the second quarter of 2026 its revenue reached $164.2 million, more than double a year earlier, and colocation revenue jumped to $136.7 million from $10.6 million. The company had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in December 2022 and emerged in January 2024. Its shares traded at $14.43 as of October 29, 2026, and lost 33.01% of their value over the prior 12 months.

The company has locked in about 1.1 gigawatts of contracted power capacity, representing more than $24 billion in future revenue. Roughly 590 megawatts across six sites is committed to CoreWeave, and AMD committed to an initial 530 megawatts across five sites under 15-year leases worth more than $14 billion, with an option to expand to as much as 2.5 gigawatts. By mid-July 2026, Core Scientific had 437 megawatts of CoreWeave capacity ready to bill, with four of its five campuses finished ahead of schedule. The next milestone is getting the Pecos site ready for AMD in the first half of 2027.

Overall gross margin was 43% and colocation margin was 59%, while adjusted EBITDA rose to $41.1 million from $8.9 million in the prior quarter. Core Scientific reported a net loss of about $1.16 billion in the second quarter, mostly from a $1.05 billion non-cash accounting charge tied to warrants linked to CoreWeave and AMD. To fund expansion it issued $3.3 billion in secured notes at a 7.75% interest rate due in 2031, and the initial AMD build-out alone is expected to cost roughly $6 billion. The company has also disclosed a material weakness in its financial reporting and restated some past results.

Wall Street price targets range from $30 to $38, while a more cautious estimate put fair value closer to $28, and KBW downgraded the stock to Hold. CoreWeave made two failed buyout attempts, a $5.75-per-share cash offer rejected in 2024 and a roughly $9 billion all-stock offer valued at about $20.40 per share that shareholders voted down in October 2025. About 26.96% of Core Scientific's float is sold short, and 75 hedge fund portfolios held the stock at the end of the second quarter, down from 81. The company warns that equipment failures and service interruptions could disrupt customers, damage its reputation and reduce revenue.

Articles.Title: Core Scientific (CORZ) vs. CIFR and WULF: Can Its Shift From Bitcoin Mining to AI Colocation Unlock Long-Term Value?

stories.Headline: ServiceNow CFO says AI disruption to enterprise software narrative is false
stories.Summary:
ServiceNow Chief Financial Officer and President Gina Mastantuono said in an interview with Seeking Alpha that the narrative of AI disrupting enterprise software is false. She said every business and industry needs a harness for AI, and that enterprise is very different. The interview was published on October 31, 2026. ServiceNow reported third-quarter results in which revenue grew above 20%, but its shares fell 27% after the company gave shortfalls in fourth-quarter cRPO and subscription growth guidance.

Analysts see robust underlying growth despite the weaker subscription guidance, with low-20% revenue growth implied for the fourth quarter and around 19% for FY27. They cite timing and accounting factors behind the weaker cRPO guidance. AI activity is strong, with nnACV growing 65% year over year, which prompted higher 2026 ACV guidance. The company cites accelerating enterprise adoption and AI pulling demand for core workloads.

Mastantuono is responsible for the comments, as the company's Chief Financial Officer and President. She said that every business and industry needs a harness for AI. She also said that enterprise is very different. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the analyst views and the company's guidance.

Articles.Title: ServiceNow CFO says AI disruption to enterprise software narrative is false

stories.Headline: NAMI joins Common Sense Media on youth AI safety standards
stories.Summary:
The National Alliance on Mental Illness has joined the Youth AI Safety Institute at Common Sense Media as a standards steering partner, according to a report published on 1 November 2026. NAMI is a US mental health organization that works through more than 650 local affiliates and 49 state organizations. It joins Crisis Text Line as a steering partner in the institute's first standards program, which deals with what the institute calls red-line severe harms. The partnership was reported by Emma Thompson of EdTech Innovation Hub. The work will focus on how AI systems should respond when young people experience severe mental health crises, including suicidal ideation and psychosis.

It will also examine when those systems should connect a young person with a trusted adult. The initial standards and their methodology are scheduled for publication in 2027. NAMI will bring the perspectives of people affected by mental illness, including young people and families, so the standards account for family members, peers and community support. Robbie Torney, Head of AI and Digital Assessments at the Youth AI Safety Institute, said NAMI knows how to build connections and care in communities. He said the institute wants NAMI's insight on how AI products can steer young people who need support toward real help.

Dr. Christine M. Crawford, NAMI's Chief Medical Officer, said the response a young person gets from AI in a moment of distress can have real consequences. She said young people deserve tools that prioritize their safety and connect them with people who can provide the right kind of mental health support and care. The partnership adds to NAMI's separate work on how AI systems respond to mental health questions. NAMI is collaborating with Dr. John Torous and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center to develop independent benchmarks for AI tools, combining clinical evidence with lived experience. Its role in the institute will concentrate on the standards for young people, particularly how AI products handle severe mental health risks and decide when to facilitate human support.

Articles.Title: NAMI joins Common Sense Media on youth AI safety standards | ETIH EdTech News

stories.Headline: EXPLAINED | What’s Eating McDonald’s in the US? McRib, AI and the Value-Meal Battle
stories.Summary:
A federal judge in Chicago allowed key claims in a proposed consumer class action over the McRib to proceed on October 30, 2026. Four consumers filed the original complaint in December 2025. They argue that the word Rib, the patty's ridges and the advertising together suggest a particular cut of pork. McDonald's disputes the allegations and says it has been transparent about ingredients.

Judge April Perry rejected McDonald's attempt to end the entire case at an early stage, while dismissing some claims. She considered it premature to conclude that a reasonable customer could not expect rib meat. The plaintiffs still need evidence to prove their case. The McRib debuted in 1981, and McDonald's told USA TODAY it would return to selected US cities from October 27 this year.

A separate October 2 complaint alleges that McDonald's illegally coordinated prices through a system using nonpublic restaurant data. McDonald's October 1 response says recommendations concern individual restaurants, franchisees choose their prices, and the tool does not determine what an individual customer pays. For April to June 2026, US comparable sales increased 0.8%, while comparable guest counts fell. McDonald's appointed Skye Anderson as US president in August.

McDonald's currently advertises an Under $3 Menu, $4 breakfast meal deals and lunch-and-dinner bundles starting at $5. Its September NEXT strategy plans approximately $5 billion in partnering support through 2030. Westlife Foodworld, an Indian McDonald's operator, reported 10.1% same-store sales growth for July to September 2026. The McRib claims that survived dismissal must now be tested through evidence.

Articles.Title: EXPLAINED | What’s Eating McDonald’s in the US? McRib, AI and the Value-Meal Battle

stories.Headline: Students across Boston walkout of class to demand AI freeze
stories.Summary:
Dozens of students, professors and activists around Boston walked out of school and work on Oct. 20 to demand an immediate freeze on artificial intelligence development, gathering outside the Massachusetts State House. The demonstration was organized by the Massachusetts AI Action Network, or MAIAN, Irreplaceable and other anti-AI advocacy groups, and the walkout began at 1 p.m. Students from many Boston-area schools took part, including Boston University, Wellesley College and Northeastern University. Demonstrators chanted that the current pace is not sustainable and that they are not replaceable.

The protesters pointed to safety risks, AI agents going rogue, cognitive offloading in schools, mass surveillance and the environmental impacts of data centers. Irreplaceable's website says the group is forming a people's movement so that everyone, not just a handful of Silicon Valley billionaires, has a say in the future. Ryan Baylon, a computer science master's student at Northeastern who helped organize the event, said MAIAN is advocating for a slowing down or heavy regulation of AI capabilities until people know how to use it safely. He also backed strong AI regulations called for by Gov. Maura Healey as part of the Mass Wins Act, saying they would be the strongest in the country if passed, with provisions including catastrophic risk safety plans, independent audits, risk and safety incident reports and whistleblower protections.

Gretchen Krueger, an AI policy researcher at Harvard and a former OpenAI researcher, said she left OpenAI two and a half years ago, disturbed by the lack of basic safety standards. She said AI should not be used to regulate itself, explaining that dominant AI companies lean on AI to trust AI to keep AI safe while allowing the technology's use by the U.S. military abroad. Matthew Bach, president of the Massachusetts Teachers Association and a teacher of more than 25 years, told the crowd that because of AI, education is becoming a product sold by big tech, and the protesters answered with a resounding "Shame!" He said ed-tech and AI amount to an enclosure of the commons that seeks to commodify, privatize and turn public education into a product to sell back to the public.

Student protesters said they have noticed cognitive decline among classmates from overusing AI. William Kramer, a second-year math major at Northeastern, said he is concerned about the implications for the future of mathematics, Northeastern and education and life everywhere, describing almost 0% participation, lectures often ignored and students entering practice problems into AI. A 2025 study from the Center for Strategic Corporate Foresight and Sustainability at SBS Swiss Business School found a significant negative correlation between frequent use of AI tools and critical thinking abilities. Olivia Colvin, a first-year acting major at Boston University, said she started realizing about two years ago how terrible AI was for her brain and how nobody wanted to learn anymore. Baylon said he agrees AI is great and can do a lot of things, which is precisely why he is worried, and as the walkout drew to a close, David Green, organizing director at the nonprofit Partners in Democracy, urged attendees to mobilize beyond the demonstration by voting in the upcoming midterm elections.

Articles.Title: Students across Boston walkout of class to demand AI freeze

stories.Headline: Over 80% of Roblox's Top 100 Games are AI-Asissted, Topping 70,000 AI Games
stories.Summary:
Roblox published a shareholder letter saying that AI-enabled game creation, automation in code generation and AI supported asset creation have led to an explosion of content since it launched its AI assisted game builder tools. The letter says over 80% of its top 100 games by hours played in September were AI assisted. The number of games created with its Build generative AI platform topped 70,000 since the second quarter. Use of Roblox's AI tools for game development more than tripled among top creators.

Roblox's Build launched in late July 2026 and lets creators use AI to generate games and content for the platform in a mobile-first experience. It is available to age-verified users nine years old and older, while published AI-generated games are available to users 16 and older. Since its alpha launch in New Zealand, Singapore, Serbia and Thailand, more than 500,000 users have used Build and have published over 70,000 games. In the third quarter, two games created almost entirely with AI broke into the top 20 Roblox game ranking by concurrent player count.

In the letter, Roblox says it is launching a Universal Player initiative that would let developers import an existing console, PC or mobile game into Roblox. The company says this would let it replicate the success it has had with its under 18 users with its 18 and over cohort, implying the generative AI tools have been most popular with under 18s. In the third quarter of 2026, 26% of Roblox's daily active users were 18 to 34, while the under-18 group made up 18% of its daily active users for the quarter. In August 2026, Roblox was accused by the US Chairman of the Committee on the Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism of prioritizing revenue and engagement metrics over the safety and well-being of children.
